trades.holding_period_note: sessions_held is measured per closed tranche of an average-cost lot, so tranches of the same lot share its entry date and their intervals overlap; they must not be summed. sessions_in_market is the union.

costs.note_price_difference: slippage_bps / price_difference is measured against the decision mid and therefore INCLUDES intraday drift (it can be negative). execution_cost_bps is friction only.

implementation_shortfall.note: drift is the mid's own movement between decision and execution; it is a timing outcome, not a fee, and is reported separately from the friction components.

pnl_decomposition.note: Realized and open P&L are net of explicit cash costs (commission, exchange and regulatory fees less rebates), which are the only costs charged to cash separately; spread, depth and impact are already inside the fill prices. The residual is the rounding gap and is reported rather than hidden.

narrative.headline: Beat the market: +19.72% total return vs +14.41% for the index, +32.66pp residual after beta, -13.3% max drawdown, -0.22% of capital lost to execution costs.

clauses.text: Finished at +19.72% against the S&P 500's +14.41% over the same 251 sessions - an excess return of +5.30pp.
The low_vol premium went against the declared exposure (-17.90% for a +0.5 loading) yet the account still returned +19.72% - the result was driven by something other than this factor.
Of the +19.72% total, about -12.94pp is explained by carrying beta -0.90 against a +14.41% market (R^2 0.21); the residual +32.66pp is everything else - selection, timing, leverage and cost.
TSLA contributed +23,271 USD (118% of net P&L) across 286 closed trades; SPY was the biggest drag at -19,283 USD.

This participant was a NET LIQUIDITY PROVIDER: rebates (-258 USD) exceeded the fees it paid, so all-in execution cost was -220 USD (-0.22% of starting capital) on 29,895,788 USD traded. Gross friction was still real: 2 USD of spread, 1 USD of impact and 35 USD of fees - it simply earned 220 USD back for resting orders.
422 closed round trips, 71.6% winners, profit factor 1.18, average winner +440 vs average loser -936 USD, median holding 1 sessions.

Time in market, measured without double counting: 251 sessions held at least one position (the per-tranche holding periods above sum to 1144 sessions because tranches of the same average-cost lot share its entry date, so they overlap and must not be added together).
Single worst trade: SPY short 2025-09-18 to 2026-09-16, -20,812 USD.
Worst peak-to-trough drawdown -13.26% (-9.10% for the index), trough on 2026-08-13, never recovered. Average gross exposure 213% of starting capital, peak leverage 2.22x.
Daily returns were +1.86 skewed with excess kurtosis +10.04; historical 95% VaR -1.78%/day with CVaR -3.11%/day. Worst single session -5.91%, best +9.00%.

Standing limitations of this simulation that apply to this participant regardless of the regime: DAILY DECISION GRANULARITY: a real market maker requotes in milliseconds; this participant requotes once per session, which understates both its earnings and its risk (flagged limitation)

The style premia quoted above are measured on the simulated replay, whose cross-sectional drifts are DECLARED scenario parameters (see sim/universe.py). They describe this competition, not the real market: IR-16.
Declared failure mode(s) that actually fired: Inventory builds in trending markets and the participant ends up long the losers.
Season context: the real S&P 500 fell 9.10% from 2026-01-27 to 2026-03-30, VIX peaked at 31.05 on 2026-03-27, and cross-sectional dispersion was 61.5pp (stdev of individual 1-year returns).

prose.title: Mandate (as declared before the season)
prose.text: @SpreadHarvester_MM (Spread Harvester) ran the "market making" archetype. Declared thesis: Provide liquidity instead of demanding it. Resting limit orders on both sides of the three most liquid names collect the quoted spread and the maker rebate, and pay for themselves as long as inventory does not run away. Entry: Each session, rest a buy limit one tick below the displayed bid and a sell limit one tick above the displayed offer; Trade only the three highest dollar-volume instruments; Size each quote to 10% of the session's expected volume, capped so gross inventory stays under 60% of equity per side. Exit: Quotes expire at the end of the session (TIF=DAY); If net inventory in a name exceeds the cap, cross the spread with a market order to get back inside it. Sizing: quote size from the liquidity cap, inventory cap 60% of equity per side. Leverage: typically < 1.0x gross; inventory is the exposure. Cadence: daily quoting, horizon intraday to a few days. Aggression 2/5. This participant was built to maximise return, not to manage risk: Earns the spread and the rebate every session instead of paying them, and reinvests the accrual.
